reference_sql:
SELECT category_id, product_id, unit_cost_eur,
       ROUND(CUME_DIST() OVER (PARTITION BY category_id ORDER BY unit_cost_eur), 3) AS cost_share
FROM products
WHERE category_id BETWEEN 1 AND 6
alternatives:
SELECT p.category_id, p.product_id, p.unit_cost_eur,
       ROUND((SELECT COUNT(*) FROM products p2 WHERE p2.category_id = p.category_id AND p2.unit_cost_eur <= p.unit_cost_eur) * 1.0
             / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM products p3 WHERE p3.category_id = p.category_id), 3) AS cost_share
FROM products p
WHERE p.category_id BETWEEN 1 AND 6

SELECT category_id, product_id, unit_cost_eur,
       ROUND(COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY category_id ORDER BY unit_cost_eur RANGE BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) * 1.0
             / COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY category_id), 3) AS cost_share
FROM products
WHERE category_id BETWEEN 1 AND 6

other_way.tradeoff: Counting the cheaper products with subqueries shows what the share means, but CUME_DIST works it out in one pass.

SELECT category_id, product_id, unit_cost_eur, cost_share
FROM (
  SELECT category_id, product_id, unit_cost_eur,
         ROUND(CUME_DIST() OVER (PARTITION BY category_id ORDER BY unit_cost_eur), 3) AS cost_share
  FROM products
  WHERE category_id BETWEEN 1 AND 6
